_comment_1: PRE-REGISTERED ACCEPTANCE CUTOFF for the AI card-generation eval.
_comment_2: Committed BEFORE any card is generated or scored. The commit ORDER is the evidence; see git log for this file's first commit versus the first commit containing generated cards or eval results.
_comment_3: BUILD-DOC 7.4. Do not edit this file after generation has run. If it must change, add a new file and record why in BRAINLIFT.md section 8 -- never amend this one.

reasoning.min_correct_and_useful: 0.80 is set below what a confident vendor would claim and above what an unreviewed generator typically achieves, so the test can fail. A threshold nobody could miss is not a threshold.
reasoning.max_wrong: 0.05 is deliberately the strictest of the three. A factually wrong card in exam prep is not merely unhelpful -- it teaches the wrong answer, and the student cannot tell. This is the category that would justify withholding the feature on its own.
reasoning.max_correct_but_bad_teaching: 0.15 is looser because the failure is recoverable: the student loses time, not accuracy. It is tracked separately rather than folded into 'correct' because collapsing it would let a generator pass by producing technically-true, useless cards.

on_failure: If any bound is breached, the AI generation feature is NOT shipped enabled by default, and the result is reported in BRAINLIFT.md section 8 as measured. The app must still compute and display all three scores with AI off -- that path is tested independently.
preconditions: The leakage check (BUILD-DOC 7.5) must run and show clean BEFORE any eval number here is reported. Leaked test data zeroes this score, so it gates everything downstream.
Every generated note must carry a resolvable source_id and character span, enforced as a BUILD ERROR rather than a lint.
